- When sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2 days above true peak.
- If sentiment is consistently neutral or negative, model underestimates; add 3–7% to forecast to account for mean reversion or hidden demand.
- Model frequently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon; apply 1–3% downward correction for days 1–7.
- If sentiment history shows no recent positive signals, model tends to underestimate; adjust upward by 5–10% for first 3–5 days of forecast.
- Model often fails to capture downward momentum after 10–15 days; apply exponential decay correction (e.g., 0.95 multiplier per day) for later forecast days.
